minutes.headline: Park Commission adopted a dog policy for park properties, endorsed adding Marshall Park to the sewer district, and approved the Marshall Park master plan RFP.
minutes.summary: The commission met Rob Thompson, the acting recreation director, then voted to approve the April minutes, the park dog regulations, a Town Meeting article adding Marshall Park to the sewer service area, and the Marshall Park master plan RFP with edits. It also decided to give Little League a Thursday deadline to supply porta-potty paperwork and sent a stern reminder about the locked dumpster. School field-use fees and the Marshall track were also discussed.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park septic, piping and building money
budget_items.what_was_said: Money for septic, piping, building and possibly fixtures is already available without fundraising; the work will go as far as the available funds take it.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park master plan RFP scope and budget
budget_items.what_was_said: Tasks two and three were removed from the RFP, partly over whether the budget would allow a modified task two.
The RFP asks consultants for sample projects with design and construction cost in a range; it is a qualification, not a request for a number from the commission.
A member said programming was cancelled when field charges pushed costs above revenue; the draft school policy waives rental fees but still charges custodial and related costs.
A preliminary cost assessment was received for beaver control at Marshall Pond; no figure was stated.

decisions.decision: Rob Oliva will ask about some form of recognition at Marshall for the all-star team.
The chair will send verification of the sewer vote to the town.
The Marshall track resurfacing is pushed into the master plan rather than a simple fix.
The dog regulations are to be posted on the MyRec page and at Fitzgerald, Marshall and McNally.
RFP edits agreed: athletic facilities listed above parking, stationary pavilion(s) plus picnic/memorial areas, skate park size changed to 5,000-10,000 sq ft.
Little League gets until 9 a.m. Thursday to supply porta-potty documentation, with removal if not.
A stern warning to lock the dumpster, reminding of the November 1 removal date; no removal yet.
Next meeting is October 27 with the beach coordinator recap, skate park and Little League invited.

what_happened.line: The Park Commission approved its dog regulations for park properties, with the town counsel's edits, on a roll call vote.
It voted to recommend to Town Meeting a warrant article adding Marshall Park to the sewer service area map.
It approved the Marshall Park master plan RFP with edits; the chair and vice chair will do a final review before it goes out.
It voted to give Little League until 9 a.m. Thursday to supply porta-potty paperwork, or the porta-potty is removed.
The commission sent a stern warning to lock the dumpster, with the November 1 removal date restated and no removal yet.

why_it_matters: The sewer article is a vote residents will likely be asked to take at Town Meeting, and it affects what can be built at Marshall Park.
The master plan RFP starts the process that will shape Marshall Park, including facilities such as a skate park and pavilion, and the money for them.
The new dog rules apply to town park properties and are to be posted at Fitzgerald, Marshall and McNally.
watch_next: The next meeting is October 27, with the beach coordinator recap and the skate park and Little League groups invited.
Town Meeting vote on the warrant article adding Marshall Park to the sewer service area.
